profile.campus: Hillsboro, Washington County, Oregon (QTS Hillsboro 3 campus)
profile.address: 23440 NE Pubols St, North Hillsboro, OR 97124
profile.reading:
Per Data Center Dynamics' 2020 coverage of QTS's Hillsboro 3 campus opening, this North Hillsboro site (reverse-geocoded to 23440 NE Pubols St) is part of a mega-scale campus first announced in 2018, planned for five data centers totaling 250+ MW across more than 1 million sq ft; Phase 1 opened October 2, 2020 with a 158,000 sq ft building and 24 MW of capacity (the first 4.5MW hall was fully leased to an unnamed cloud software provider at opening), following a February 2020 groundbreaking on a 27MW phase. The campus connects to the QTS Hillsboro Network Access Point (NAP) and the Hillsboro Ring, which per DCD's reporting serves 14 data centers in the area.

QTS was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, and was taken private in a roughly $10 billion Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT)-led acquisition completed August 31, 2021, per Blackstone's own press release; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer. Hillsboro, in Oregon's Washington County, is one of three QTS campuses in the immediate area (Hillsboro 1, 2, and 3) and part of the Portland metro's broader "Silicon Forest" data center cluster, drawing power from the regional grid and, per QTS's own Hillsboro 3 materials, offering customers 100% renewable energy through power purchase agreements.

Hillsboro's "Silicon Forest" data center cluster grew out of the area's legacy semiconductor and electronics manufacturing base (anchored historically by Intel's large Washington County campuses), which left behind substantial fiber infrastructure and a skilled technical workforce that later attracted data center operators; the Hillsboro Herald, a local outlet, has reported on the scale of competing data center construction projects in the immediate area as the industrial land base has shifted from chip fabrication toward digital infrastructure. QTS's Hillsboro presence, spread across three separate campuses (Hillsboro 1, 2, and 3), reflects a broader industry pattern in Oregon's Washington County of sequential campus expansion by the same operator as adjacent land becomes available, similar to the multi-campus patterns seen for QTS in Northern Virginia and for other operators in this registry's Loudoun County and Quincy, Washington clusters.

reading.body:
QTS Data Center—Hillsboro 3 is a planned two-building campus in Oregon's Willamette Valley data center cluster, designed for 100+ MW of total power capacity across 44 acres. The operator has not published per-building power allocations or individual IT load figures, only this combined campus total. If the full 100 MW reaches production as a colocation facility at typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the campus could support roughly 2,500 racks, though this is an assumption about end-use that the operator does not confirm.

Oregon has 133 mapped data center facilities, of which only 8 publish power capacity figures totaling 156.6 MW. This campus, if completed at its stated 100+ MW capacity, would exceed the published capacity of all other facilities in the state combined and rank as by far the largest in Oregon by announced power budget. The ranking reflects only published figures from operator spec pages. Hillsboro itself hosts major facilities from multiple operators and is an established data center hub.

The facility is still in development with no confirmed individual building addresses published by the operator. QTS, acquired by Blackstone in 2021, is a large-scale data center provider, but no tenant commitments, certifications, or operational timeline for this campus are stated in public specifications. Whether and when this capacity reaches the grid remains unconfirmed.
